en: The Eight Verses of Prayer to Śrī Nṛsiṃha Sarasvatī
He who was born as the son of the wife of a twice-born man named Ṛtakṛt, and whose name was Smara—may that blessed ascetic Nṛsiṃhasarasvatī be my supreme and most excellent refuge. 1.
From birth he recited the *praṇava*; though existing in a state of limited perception, he was esteemed as one who had transcended it.
That venerable ascetic Nṛsiṃhasarasvatī is my supreme and most excellent refuge. 2.
He who restored to life the son of a deceased Brahmin and milked the barren buffalo-cow—he, the blessed Yati Sarasvatī Nṛsiṃha, is my supreme and excellent refuge. 3.
He revealed his own form to the ascetic and destroyed the pride of the twice-born;
that venerable ascetic Nṛsiṃha Sarasvatī is my supreme and most excellent refuge. 4.
For even to one whose beloved wife has died, he bestowed the good fortune of being honored;
that venerable ascetic Nṛsiṃhasarasvatī is my supreme and excellent refuge. 5.
He who increases the prosperity of his own lineage and also causes the growth of the lineage of his devoted wife—that venerable ascetic Nṛsiṃhasarasvatī is my supreme and most excellent refuge. (6)
He who extracted the *kusuru* seeds from dry wood and purified the *kuṣṭha* from leprosy—that venerable ascetic Nṛsiṃhasarasvatī is my supreme and most excellent refuge. 7.
In the city named Amarā, there is the bestower of boons upon the yoginīs; that blessed ascetic Nṛsiṃhasarasvatī, who is the master of all the yoginīs, is my supreme and most excellent refuge. (8)
Thus ends the Śrī Nṛsiṃhasarasvatī Stotra, composed by the venerable Paṇḍitācārya Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
